title: Tiered burst quotas, soft/hard rate limits and overage billing policy
creator: Amira Hassan
description: PRD for introducing tiered burst quotas and a clear soft vs hard rate limit behavior across Redwood hosted and dedicated plans, plus a standardized overage billing flow. Goal: reduce unexpected rate-limit errors for new customers, allow short-term traffic bursts without immediate hard failures, and provide transparent automatic billing for overages with opt-out. This should align Console UI, API responses, and billing ledger semantics. Stakeholders: PM, Billing, Console, Runtime, Legal. Constraints: must be compatible with existing usage metering pipeline (token-level and embedding units), not add more than 15% latency to rate-limit checks, and respect Dedicated customers who require strict isolation and manual overage consent.
requirements: Define three quota layers per plan: baseline steady-state quota (monthly window), burst buffer (short-term allowance measured in tokens and requests), and per-second soft rate limit
Soft limits should throttle with controlled retries and informative headers, not immediate 429 hard failures until burst buffer exhausted or soft limit exceeded for >30s
Hard limits remain enforced for safety (abuse/fraud) and Dedicated customers can opt for hard-only behavior
Overage-enabled plans will automatically bill at a defined overage rate after monthly quota exhaustion; opt-out plans will block traffic and show a grace window notification
Console: show real-time quota burn, projected date-to-exhaust at current rate, burst buffer usage, and one-click opt-in for overage billing
API responses must include: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Burst-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and a machine-readable reason for throttling (soft_throttle | hard_limit | quota_exhausted)

Billing: invoice line items for overage must list units consumed, unit price, and associated plan id; prorated mid-cycle plan upgrades should recompute remaining monthly quota and adjust overage thresholds
Edge cases: embeddings vs generation units must count against separate quota buckets but share burst buffer; server-side aggregation must reconcile multi-region requests into a single monthly bucket
scope_changes: 2025-02-20: Removed initial scope to add per-customer tunable burst size due to complexity; instead plan-level tiers only
2025-02-24: Added requirement that Dedicated customers can elect for billing opt-in via signed agreement (legal requirement)
2025-03-01: Shifted Embeddings accounting to a separate quota with shared burst buffer after feedback from Platform customers
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts and enforces plan-tiered quotas in staging for hosted plans and logs quota decisions to Console appropriately
Soft throttles return 429 with Retry-After and X-Quota headers for up to 30s of sustained excess; after 30s, behaviors degrade to hard limit as configured
Console displays burst buffer usage and projected exhaustion in the usage pane for all customers; values match billing metering within 1% over a 24h sample
E2E tests covering token-level metering, burst buffer exhaustion, and mid-cycle upgrades exist and pass in CI
Billing exports include overage line items with plan id and unit pricing and reconcile to invoices in staging environment
billing_acceptance_criteria: When a hosted account exhausts monthly baseline and has overage enabled, an overage invoice line is created automatically at the next billing run and shows items: units, unit price, and total
If overage is disabled, customer receives console notification and API calls are blocked with a clear error code: quota_exhausted_no_overage
Grace period: accounts that newly enable overage mid-cycle receive a configurable 48h grace window where overage is tracked but not billed; billing shows a 'grace' flag in staging exports
Proration: when a customer upgrades mid-cycle to a higher plan, remaining quota is prorated and overage thresholds are recomputed; tests must show correct ledger adjustments
Billing ledger and Console usage must reconcile within 2% for tokens and 3% for embeddings across a 7-day synthetic test

2025-02-22: Legal confirmed Dedicated customers require signed opt-in for auto-overage; added to scope
2025-02-27: Console mockups (drive link) uploaded showing new burst buffer UI and one-click overage toggle
2025-03-03: Billing engineering proposed invoice line schema change to include 'grace' boolean; accepted for staging only
